extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, SBE-FPs, FFE States, QHP issuers, insurers, agents/brokers, and other health policy stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the proposed regulatory criteria and standards in an HHS/CMS proposed rule concerning Marketplace program integrity, special enrollment, hardship exemptions, network adequacy, ECP reviews, and State-level improper payment measurement. Intended to support notice-and-comment responses and implementation planning by Exchanges, issuers, and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium payment threshold policy (fixed-dollar and gross-premium percentage-based thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to continue limiting the fixed-dollar and gross-premium percentage-based thresholds beyond PY 2026, given concerns about program integrity and consumer outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notes these thresholds could allow enrollees to remain in coverage for extended periods without paying at least some premium, increase the risk that improper enrollments remain undetected (e.g., false contact information), and lead to accumulation of large debt where gross-premium percentage thresholds apply. In contrast, the long-established net percentage-based threshold ensures enrollees must always pay at least some premium to avoid delinquency or loss of coverage. HHS seeks comment on allowing the policies to sunset, extending the rescission for another fixed time or permanently, and on whether State Exchanges should be granted flexibility to adopt one or both thresholds even if unavailable on the Federal platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: 150 percent FPL SEP prohibition (sunset removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove §155.420(d)(16) and related conforming provisions to permanently prohibit Exchanges from offering the 150 percent FPL Special Enrollment Period after PY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: the 150 percent FPL SEP previously enabled APTC-eligible individuals at ≤150% FPL to enroll and change plans monthly; earlier regulation required applicable percentage of zero for eligibility but that requirement was removed. The WFTC legislation (section 71304) amended section 36B of the Code so that income-based SEPs (based solely on expected household income relative to FPL) render a plan not a QHP for PTC purposes effective Jan 1, 2026. HHS reasons allowing the SEP provides no additional value (no APTC allowed) and could harm APTC-eligible consumers because payment of APTC to a plan is prohibited if any enrollee enrolled through an income-based SEP. HHS seeks comment on this proposal and related conforming removals to plan category/effective date language.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEPV scope and verification threshold (at least 75% of new enrollments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproposal to remove restriction limiting Federal platform SEPV to Loss of MEC and to require Exchanges on the Federal platform to conduct Special Enrollment Period Verification (SEPV) for at least 75 percent of new enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS finalized these policies in the 2025 rule but included a December 31, 2026 sunset; the reproposal (without a sunset) follows a court stay. The 75% threshold is to be calculated based on enrollment through all SEPs in the prior plan year, allowing Exchanges flexibility to choose which SEP types to verify (so as not to require verification of very low-utilization SEPs). Rationale includes GAO findings on risks from self-attestation, historical SEPV processing performance (e.g., 1–3 day review times in PY2017, high verification success rates), and observed enrollment shifts after resuming Loss of MEC verification—suggesting intentional attestation shifts to avoid verification, potentially driven by agents/brokers (86% of SEP enrollments are through agents/brokers). HHS seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment pend and cancellation for SEPs under verification
rubrics_metrics.description: For SEPs that are being verified, Exchanges will pend the consumer's enrollment until eligibility is verified; inability to verify leads to cancellation (enrollment terminated before coverage effectuated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an Exchange pends an enrollment due to SEPV, the enrollment is not effectuated until verification is completed. If verification fails, any plan selection under that SEP is canceled and will not result in enrollment. This mechanism is part of the proposed SEPV expansion and the 75% verification threshold policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardship exemption substantive criteria (§155.605(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange must grant a hardship exemption when the Exchange determines the individual experienced specified financial/domestic circumstances preventing obtaining coverage, including three statutory criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §155.605(d) currently requires granting a hardship exemption for at least the month before, the month(s) during which, and the month after a specific event if: (1) the individual experienced financial or domestic circumstances (including unexpected natural or human-caused events) causing a significant, unexpected increase in essential expenses preventing QHP coverage; (2) purchasing a QHP would cause serious deprivation of food, shelter, clothing or other necessities; or (3) the individual experienced other circumstances that prevented obtaining coverage under a QHP. States may process exemptions or delegate processing to HHS; most States delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardship exemption expansion to those ineligible for APTC/CSR due to projected income (§155.605(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §155.605(d)(1) to codify expansion of hardship exemption eligibility to individuals ineligible for APTC or CSR because projected household income is below 100 percent or above 250 percent FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS previously issued guidance (Sept 4, 2025) expanding eligibility for certain consumers; this proposal would make the change nationwide for all States to improve access to catastrophic coverage for consumers for whom purchasing a QHP relative to a catastrophic plan could cause financial hardship. HHS cites premium growth (e.g., average monthly premiums rising from $244 in 2013 to $779 in 2026) as justification and proposes that States continue to have discretion to adopt the expanded criteria or delegate processing to HHS; technical assistance would be provided. HHS seeks comment on the proposal and the proposed effective date if finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority for network adequacy standards (§155.1050)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to restore network adequacy authority to State Exchanges and SBE-FPs by removing federal requirements that State Exchanges impose quantitative time and distance standards at least as stringent as FFE standards for plan years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes removing §155.1050(a)(2)(i) and (ii) (time/distance quantitative standards and required quantitative reviews) and returning to a requirement that State Exchanges ensure each QHP provides sufficient access to providers in a manner meeting applicable standards in §156.230(a)(1)(ii)/(iii) for network plans or proposed §156.236(a) for non-network plans. Rationale: many State Exchanges already had adequate standards and varied approaches (time/distance, appointment wait times, provider-to-enrollee ratios) and are better positioned to account for local provider supply and geography. HHS also proposes adding §155.1050(d) to specify an Effective Provider Access Review Program for certain FFE States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program (§155.1050(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and deferral framework for FFE States that elect to conduct provider access reviews and be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §155.1050(d)(1)-(4) would, beginning PY 2027, allow HHS to defer provider access reviews for QHP issuers applying through an FFE to States that elect to conduct such reviews and demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity. Proposed requirements include ensuring in-network providers include Essential Community Providers (ECPs) per §156.235; maintaining a network sufficient in number and types of providers (including mental health and SUD specialists) so services are accessible without unreasonable delay; and ensuring non-network plans provide a sufficient choice of providers who accept the benefit amount as payment in full. HHS also proposes factors states must satisfy to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program and invites comment on appropriate transparency of processes and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Essential Community Provider (ECP) Review Program (§155.1051)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to allow FFE States (including States performing plan management) to elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews for issuer plans applying for QHP certification through an FFE, provided the State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that meet HHS-established criteria to be considered to have an Effective ECP Review Program would be permitted to conduct ECP certification reviews for plans with or without a provider network. HHS references section III.E.11. for greater detail and proposes this change beginning PY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement (SEIPM) program (proposed subpart Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to establish a SEIPM program to develop State Exchange improper payment estimates and provide an accurate methodology for calculating and reporting improper payment rates in HHS' Agency Financial Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Payment Integrity Information Act (PIIA), HHS determined APTC payments administered by State Exchanges are susceptible to significant improper payments. Proposed subpart Q would specify a methodology, require State Exchanges to provide HHS access to certain State Exchange data (including eligibility determinations and enrollment information), and enable consistent calculation and reporting. States found to have significant improper payments (per PIIA thresholds) could be required to develop corrective action plans (CAPs). The proposed SEIPM process could allow States to satisfy certain independent external programmatic audit requirements and reduce duplication with §155.1200(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual independent external programmatic audits and reporting (§155.1200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing and proposed requirements for State Exchanges to engage independent qualified auditing entities to perform annual external financial and programmatic audits and to submit annual reporting materials to HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key annual reporting requirements at §155.1200(b) include: (1) a financial statement per generally accepted accounting principles; (2) an annual report showing compliance with Exchange requirements; and (3) performance monitoring data. Per §155.1200(c) and (d), State Exchanges must contract with an independent qualified auditing entity following Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards to perform annual audits addressing compliance with 45 CFR part 155 subparts D and E, or other applicable part 155 requirements. State Exchanges must provide HHS with audit results and CAPs to address material weaknesses or significant deficiencies; HHS monitors CAPs until resolved. The proposed SEIPM program is intended to reduce duplication with these audit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency expectations for Effective Provider Access Review Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS seeks comment on the level and form of transparency necessary and appropriate to safeguard public trust in State Effective Provider Access Review Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS is not specifying particular disclosure requirements at this time but requests public feedback on which elements of process and outputs of Effective Provider Access Review Programs should be publicly disclosed to balance transparency with operational considerations.
